newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania's Landsbergis ahead in early results.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania's Landsbergis ahead in early results.

text.p: Lithuania's independence hero Vytautas Landsbergis looked set on Monday to avenge a bitter defeat four years ago by ex-Communists as early results from parliamentary elections put his Homeland Union party in front.

With 48 of the 2,037 electoral districts counted, the Homeland Union had 25.83 percent of the vote, the Christian Democrats 17.14 and the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) of ex-Communists 13.06. The only other parties above the five percent mark were the Social Democrats with 8.37 and the Centre Union 5.02.
Sunday's elections, the second Lithuania has held since it quit the former Soviet Union, were hit by voter aparthy.
Turnout figures showed Lithuanians had failed to get excited about the elections. With two hours of voting to go, just over 50 percent of the electorate had turned out.

Landsbergis spearheaded the Baltic state's independence drive from Moscow in a struggle that helped bring down the whole Soviet empire. But a shock reversal at elections in 1992 saw voters dump him as the economy collapsed.
The Homeland Union has said it will work with the Christian Democrats, who stress traditional values in this Roman Catholic country.
